messages:
meera: heads-up: running the edge-worker quickstart (local emulation) I can see Authorization header fragments and a primary key in our debug logs when the SDK retries. this is happening only when LOG_LEVEL=debug and with AUTOINIT=true. anyone else noticing header leakage in local runs?

gabe: yikes. can you paste the lines (redact if sensitive)?

meera: pasted raw output from my local run:```2026-09-03T11:02:21.120Z DEBUG rd.request_id=rd-01 attempt=1 auth.partial=Bearer%20eyJhbGci... user.email=demo@realcorp.com route=/edge/signup
2026-09-03T11:02:21.321Z DEBUG rd.request_id=rd-02 attempt=2 sdk.retry=true auth.partial=Bearer%20eyJhbGci... message=retrying request
```

ryan: looks like two issues: (1) seed data includes real-looking emails and the auth header is being serialized into structured attrs at debug level, (2) retries are generating new rd.request_id values instead of preserving the canonical request id, so logs from the same logical request are split.

gabe: root cause theory: the edge runtime auto-instruments fetch/XHR and records request attributes early. our retry middleware (in the SDK) does an internal re-emit and generates a new request id per attempt. additionally, the autoinit/otel log exporter is capturing headers because we map http.req.headers to a structured attribute.

meera: repro steps I used: 1) git clone repo/sample-edge 2) cp .env.example .env (LOG_LEVEL=debug AUTOINIT=true) 3) npm ci && npm run dev:edge 4) curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" localhost:8787/edge/signup 5) tail -f logs/edge-local.log | grep "auth.partial"

ops-bot: recommended quick mitigation: set LOG_LEVEL=info in the edge quickstart, and move example emails to example.invalid. For local emulators, avoid streaming logs to external collectors.

ryan: tactical fixes: - change quickstart default to LOG_LEVEL=info - don't map full headers to export attrs by default (only expose header names in developer mode) - make SDK retry preserve request id by propagating rd.request_id through attempts instead of creating a new one.

tara: for redaction options: we can implement an OTEL LogProcessor that masks Authorization values and common PII before export. In addition, add a small middleware that strips Authorization from logs at serialization point: e.g.,```const scrubHeaders = (attrs) => { if (attrs['http.request.header.authorization']) attrs['http.request.header.authorization'] = '[REDACTED]'; return attrs; }```and register that as a pre-export processor during autoinit.

gabe: long-term SDK changes we discussed: - introduce AUTOINIT_MODE with values {off, minimal, full} so quickstarts can choose minimal instrumentation that avoids header capture - add AUTOINIT_PII_GUARD=true by default for sample apps which wires in a redact processor on init - canonicalize request id key to rd.request_id and add instructions for proxies to forward x-rd-request-id -> rd.request_id to avoid collisions.

meera: I'll open a small PR that: 1) changes quickstart envs to LOG_LEVEL=info and sample emails to example.invalid 2) registers a pre-export redact processor in the edge sample when AUTOINIT=true 3) updates the README with guidance for emulators about not using real tokens or emails.

telemetry-bot: Created ticket INF-3333: "edge quickstart: Authorization header fragments and PII at debug level; retries split request_id"  https://tracker.internal/INF-3333 :bug:

ryan: additional CI safety net: add a lightweight grep step in onboarding smoke that fails if logs contain Authorization: Bearer or email regex patterns. Example step:```- name: scan-onboarding-logs run: if grep -E "Authorization: Bearer|[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}" logs/*.log; then echo "PII or auth leaked"; exit 1; fi```

tara: agree. also add unit tests for retry behavior to assert rd.request_id is preserved across attempts and that auth headers are masked in exported attrs.

meera: assigning myself for the quick PR. I'll also ping infra to check edge emulator defaults in cloud demos.

gabe: thanks. small wins here will stop accidental leaks in demos and local dev. :white_check_mark:
